text:
clare: Heads-up — as part of this quarter's access review I ran a quick sweep and found ~14 service keys in the analytics project that haven't been used in 180+ days. Some are bound to a KMS key in keyring-prod. Thinking we should canary-delete in staging first.

nate: yikes. do we know which keys are still referenced by cron jobs or airflow?

clare: not yet. I pulled last access from GCP audit logs but there are gaps — retention for admin logs was 90d in that billing account. audit-bot shows no entries older than that.

eli: @clare can you paste the query you used? might be worth checking Storage access patterns too (some services checkpoint to buckets).

clare: query: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=\"k8s_container\" OR resource.labels.project_id=\"analytics-prod\"' --limit 1000 --freshness 365d` — but as said, logs truncated.

jenna: if logs are missing we should be careful deleting keys that have KMS grants; cross-project grants are common for the analytics ETL. Also remember we have a known issue where kms-grant events weren't ingested into the audit index for a 2-week window in nov.

nate: we should map service accounts -> key grants before any removal. I can run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` across the ring and build a diff.

clare: plan proposal: (1) identify candidate keys with zero activity in available logs; (2) build SA->KMS grant map; (3) canary disable keys in staging and watch for errors (alerts + 24h); (4) schedule deletion after 7d rollback window.

eli: add step: export list and ping app owners with a one-click rollback link. we had a fallout last year where a hidden consumer caused a job to fail for a day.

jenna: also file a short incident-runbook note that the audit-gap exists and include the linked retention policy change ticket: https://redwood.internal/infra/ops/1234 — want to avoid future blindspots.

clare: good call. I'll create a short PR with the candidate list and the canary playbook. Nate, can you run the KMS grant inventory and attach the CSV?

nate: on it. ETA 60m. I'll also grep Cloud Scheduler (`gcloud scheduler jobs list --project=analytics-prod`) and check secret manager accesses.

audit-bot: NOTICE: automated evidence check — KMS admin grant events missing between 2025-11-08 and 2025-11-22. See infra ticket #1234.

eli: once we have the CSV we should annotate each row: last_seen, kms_grant_present, owner (if unknown put `ops-oncall`). then send owners a ping template.

clare: ping template draft: "We've flagged <key> as unused in our retention window and will disable it in staging at T. Please reply if you require it to remain active. If no reply we'll proceed with removal schedule." Thoughts?

jenna: concise and safe. include link to rollback runbook and contact for rapid re-enable. add :eyes: emoji to owners ping to increase visibility.

clare: thanks. posting PR and candidate list in 1h. tagging this thread `audit:access-review/quick-canary` for tracking.

nate: once CSV is up i'll also run a small smoke-run for 3 downstream jobs to ensure no breakage in staging.

eli: LGTM. keep me posted if any owner objects — we'll escalate to product for exceptions.

clare: closing loop here later with actions and timestamps. thx :thumbsup:
